tasks.title: platform: uv workspace and per-component CI
tasks.goal: Give every team a Python workspace and a CI that lints, tests and checks contracts and ownership for each component, so teams can add packages without editing root config.
acceptance: Root pyproject.toml declares a uv workspace with members globbed as components/* and libs/*; `uv sync` succeeds on a clean checkout (paste output)

Extends the existing .github/workflows/ci.yml with jobs: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `uv run pytest` per workspace member, `python3 tools/validate_contracts.py`, `python3 tools/check_ownership.py`
Pytest markers `safety`, `hardware`, `slow` registered at the root; `hardware` and `slow` are deselected in the PR job
Jobs are path-filtered so a change in one component does not run every component's tests
Proven on the PR: link a CI run that fails on a deliberately broken test commit and passes after reverting it
uv cache enabled via astral-sh/setup-uv
out_of_scope: Creating any component package (each team creates its own)

tasks.title: platform: generate Pydantic models from contract schemas
tasks.goal: Every Python team imports one generated set of models (py_common.models) that matches contracts/schemas exactly, so no team hand-writes its own copy.
acceptance: `uv run python tools/codegen/gen_models.py` regenerates libs/py-common/src/py_common/models/ from contracts/schemas/*.schema.json
Generated models use extra='forbid'; a test parses every file in contracts/fixtures/valid/<schema>/ with its model and round-trips it (`uv run pytest libs/py-common -k fixtures`)
Every file in contracts/fixtures/invalid/ is rejected by its model, including has-allergen-field.json (test marked safety)
CI drift check: regenerating on a clean checkout produces no git diff, otherwise the job fails
The PR records which generator was used and whether cross-file $ref and the verdict if/then rules are handled; any rule not generated is enforced by a hand-written validator with a test
out_of_scope: Changing any schema (that is an RFC)

tasks.title: platform: py_common Protocols and injectable Clock
tasks.goal: Publish every interface from contracts/apis.md as typing.Protocol classes, plus a Clock, so teams code against stable signatures and replay stays deterministic.
acceptance: py_common.interfaces exposes StateClient, JevClient, LayaClient, Transcriber, Speaker, GateDriver and InteractionClassifier with the exact signatures in contracts/apis.md, typed with py_common.models
Exceptions StateUnavailable, JevUnavailable, LayaUnavailable exported from py_common.errors; ChangeEvent model for subscribe()
py_common.clock exposes a Clock protocol, SystemClock and ManualClock (advance/set); a test shows ManualClock drives t_ms deterministically
`uv run pyright libs/py-common` passes in basic mode
A test asserts each Protocol's method names match the list in contracts/apis.md, so drift is caught
out_of_scope: Any implementation, real or fake, other than ManualClock and SystemClock
Adding methods not in contracts/apis.md (raise an RFC instead)

tasks.title: platform: InMemoryStateClient and scenario loader
tasks.goal: Ship the reference fake for StateClient and a loader for scenario files, so every Python team can build and test with no database.
acceptance: py_common.fakes.InMemoryStateClient implements every StateClient method, including subscribe() delivering ChangeEvents on insert and update
Failure injection: set_unavailable(True) and fail_next(n) make methods raise StateUnavailable (test)
upsert_entities never deletes and never overwrites first_seen_t_ms (test marked safety); amendments keep prior ticket revisions (test)
list_interactions returns events ordered by t_start_ms; duplicate event_id is a no-op
py_common.scenarios.load_scenario(path) populates bins, late entities, tickets, plate bindings and events; all five files in contracts/scenarios/ load (`uv run pytest libs/py-common -k scenario`)
Scenario iteration yields events and plates-at-pass in time order

tasks.title: platform: end-to-end harness on fakes (tools/e2e)
tasks.goal: Prove the pieces fit: run each golden scenario and a typed-note ticket through intake, state, provenance and the output fakes, and compare against the expected verdicts.
acceptance: `uv run python -m tools.e2e --all-scenarios` runs every file in contracts/scenarios/ on InMemoryStateClient in rules_only mode and exits non-zero on any mismatch with `expected` (decision, allergens reached, reason codes, chain event IDs)
`uv run python -m tools.e2e --note "peanut allergy, traces matter"` goes through FakeJev, answers any questions from a scripted answer file, sends the ticket, and prints the stored Ticket
Verdicts drive ConsoleGate and ConsoleSpeaker if experience has shipped them; otherwise the harness prints the verdict and notes the missing fake
Each component is used only through its published interface or entry point; the harness imports no team internals
Output is deterministic under ManualClock (two runs, identical output, shown in the PR)

tasks.title: platform: shared StateClient contract test suite
tasks.goal: One pytest suite, parametrized over StateClient implementations, defines the behavior both the fake and the real client must have.
acceptance: py_common.testing.state_contract exposes a parametrizable suite covering every StateClient method, idempotent writes by primary key, time-ordered list_interactions, preserved first_seen_t_ms, kept ticket revisions, and StateUnavailable on failure
The suite passes against InMemoryStateClient (`uv run pytest libs/py-common -k state_contract`)
README section explains how state plugs in the real client via a fixture
out_of_scope: Running the suite against a real database (state-03 does that)

tasks.title: platform: generate TypeScript types from contract schemas
tasks.goal: Give experience generated TypeScript types for every contract message, so web apps never hand-write contract shapes.
acceptance: libs/ts-contracts with `npm run gen` that writes .d.ts types for every schema in contracts/schemas
`npx tsc --noEmit` type-checks a test file that imports every valid fixture as its generated type
CI job: regenerating produces no git diff, and tsc passes
The PR records the generator used and any schema features it could not express

tasks.title: platform: make bootstrap and seed scripts idempotent
tasks.goal: tools/bootstrap_github.sh and tools/seed_issues.py can be re-run safely, so labels, milestones, boards and backlog issues never duplicate.
acceptance: Both scripts support --dry-run that prints every action without calling GitHub
A second real run creates zero new labels, milestones or issues (paste the summary line of both runs)
seed_issues.py validates every tools/backlog/*.json against the documented shape and reports unknown blocked_by keys before creating anything
out_of_scope: Changing label names or the backlog shape (Director decision)

tasks.title: platform: lint .claude/agents definitions in CI
tasks.goal: Catch broken agent definitions before they break a launch.
acceptance: tools/check_agents.py parses the YAML frontmatter of every .claude/agents/*.md and fails on missing name or description, duplicate names, or unknown keys from a documented allowlist
Runs in CI; `python3 tools/check_agents.py` passes on main
out_of_scope: Editing agent prompts (Director owns their content)

tasks.title: platform: PR checks for cross-team and contract labels
tasks.goal: CI enforces the lane rules: a PR touching more than one team's paths needs `cross-team`, and one touching contracts/ needs `contract-change`.
acceptance: CI job runs `python3 tools/check_ownership.py --diff origin/main` and posts the touched teams in the job summary
Fails if more than one team is touched without the cross-team label, or contracts/ is touched without contract-change (uv.lock regeneration is exempt)
Demonstrated on the PR with a throwaway commit that trips the check
out_of_scope: Required-review enforcement (labels are the approval mechanism, see WORKFLOW.md)

tasks.title: platform: CI job running golden and generated scenarios
tasks.goal: Every PR touching provenance, contracts or tools/e2e runs all golden scenarios end to end, and sim-generated scenarios run nightly.
acceptance: `golden-scenarios` CI job runs `uv run python -m tools.e2e --all-scenarios` on PRs touching components/provenance/, contracts/ or tools/e2e/
Nightly scheduled job generates a batch with the sim generator and runs it through the harness; failures open or update a type:bug issue
Job summary lists each scenario with pass or fail
out_of_scope: Writing scenarios (sim, any team via PR)

tasks.title: platform: run e2e against the real StateClient
tasks.goal: Satisfy the M1 exit item that the vertical slice runs on a real local SpacetimeDB, not only the fake.
acceptance: `uv run python -m tools.e2e --all-scenarios --state real` uses state's StateClient against a local DB started by state's dev script
Results match the InMemoryStateClient run scenario by scenario
CI job installs the SpacetimeDB CLI with state's script and runs it; if the CLI cannot run on CI runners, the PR says so and the job is a documented local-only command
